decision.explanation: The provided evidence from pmid-24353160 explicitly identifies the EGFR L858R mutation as 'erlotinib-sensitive' and demonstrates that cell lines expressing this mutation (e.g., H3255) are inhibited by submicromolar concentrations of erlotinib, supporting the claim that EGFR L858R is a predictive biomarker for sensitivity/response to Erlotinib in lung non-small cell carcinoma.

citations.quote: In addition, we used gefitinib/erlotinib-sensitive (L858R and exon 19 deletion mutations [delL747_S752 and delL747_P753insS]) and gefitinib/erlotinib-resistant (L858R+T790M and exon 19 deletion mutations+T790M) mutations as assay controls. . . . We created Ba/F3 cells stably expressing the aforementioned EGFR mutations. All were able to proliferate in the absence of IL3 (Sup. Fig. 1), indicating transforming ability of these mutations. We next measured proliferation in the presence of erlotinib and showed that only cells with EGFR-delL747_P753insS, L858R and the atypical A763_Y764insFQEA -

Proliferation assays with increasing concentrations of EGFR TKIs disclosed that growth of BID007, PC9, HCC827 and H3255 cells was inhibited by submicromolar concentrations of erlotinib (Fig. 3C, Sup. Table 2), gefitinib and afatinib (Sup. Table 2), indicating augmented sensitivity relative to the inhibitor-resistant H1975 cell line.
